Subject: Economics validation for MAP: token slicing + caching assumptions

Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, we want to lock the mutual action plan (MAP) items that affect go/no-go and pilot sizing, specifically the unit-economics assumptions that feed your procurement and FinOps review. I pulled together a short checklist and a first-pass sim attached. High-level asks: 

- Confirm the traffic slice we should model for the pilot (peak QPS, typical session length, and percent of sessions that hit prefetch/caching).
- Agree on two candidate prompt mixes (short/long) and a target tokens-per-session distribution.
- Validate whether the KV-cache / prefix cache can be used for the assistant use cases we discussed (PHI redaction flow and summary). If not, note fallback cache hit assumptions.
- Pick batching latency tolerances (SLOs) — these materially change tokens/$ in our simulation.

Attachments: token-econ-sim-v2.csv (first-pass sim), MAP-draft-Sunstorm-2026.pdf (MAP draft with milestones).

If you prefer, we can run a quick scoped sim with your real session traces — 1-2 hours on our side to ingest an anonymized sample. Next steps I propose: you confirm the traffic slice & caching availability by Thursday; we’ll iterate the sim and deliver a final MAP appendix with unit-econ sensitivity ranges by Tuesday next week.

Thanks,
Dylan

Dylan —

Appreciate the notes and the sim. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic slice: for the pilot we want to model a conservative healthcare slice — 30 RPS peak, median session ~120 tokens, 95th pct sessions ~800 tokens.
- Prefetch/cache: our security team has allowed a short-lived KV cache for non-PHI derived data. Anything containing PHI must bypass shared cache; we can supply a flag in the payload to indicate PHI vs non-PHI.
- Batching: clinical UX requires <200ms tail latency for suggestion flows. For async summary jobs we can accept up to 2s.

We’ll confirm with procurement on how aggressive they want the tokens/$ sensitivity baked into the SOW — should we provide the sim with a base-case and a conservative-case? Also attaching a short note from our FinOps lead (see inline).

Sara
Sara Lin
Head of Product — Digital Tools, Sunstorm Health

Looping in some quick sims. I ran three scenarios in token-econ-sim-v2.csv: base, conservative (lower cache hits / higher long-tail), and optimistic (higher cache hit + batching enabled). Notes: 

- Cache hit rate assumptions: I left non-PHI cache hit at 35% base, 20% conservative, 55% optimistic. If Sunstorm can tag the PHI flag reliably, non-PHI cache is implementable and the delta is meaningful (~22-28% tokens/$ improvement in optimistic vs conservative).
- Batching trade-offs: to hit <200ms tail we have to keep batching window small (<=20ms) which leaves less opportunity to batch; that lands us closer to the conservative case. If you can tolerate 350-400ms for some assistant responses we can enable larger batching windows and approach the optimistic numbers.
- Prefetch: prefetching the top-3 tokens for summary pipelines yielded ~12% offload to cache in the sim.

Attachment: token-econ-sim-v2.csv (updated with scenario tabs). I also added a short comment inside the MAP draft for the financial appendix.

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and clarifications. Per Ben’s sims and your constraints, here’s a short MAP appendix summary and next steps (I’ll push an updated MAP-draft-Sunstorm-2026.pdf to the Drive link):

MAP appendix (unit-econ focus):
- Traffic slice used: 30 RPS peak, median 120 tokens/session, 95th pct 800 tokens (Sunstorm confirmed).
- Cache gating: non-PHI KV cache allowed, PHI flagged traffic excluded; we used 35% base cache hit in the sim.
- Batching SLOs: suggestion flows target 200ms tail -> use small batching window (<=20ms) in pilot. Async summary flows: 2s latency -> batching window 200-400ms.
- Scenarios delivered: base, conservative (-25% cache hit), optimistic (+20% cache hit + relaxed batching).
- Financial output: tokens/$ ranges for pilot (monthly) and sensitivity to cache hit and batching. See token-econ-sim-v2.csv for numbers.

Action items & timeline (MAP milestones):
1) Procurement sign-off on pilot budget and acceptance criteria — due 2026-09-07 (Sunstorm).
2) Redwoods to deliver updated MAP appendix and finalized SOW with the conservative and base econ tables — due 2026-09-03 (Redwood).
3) Hand off anonymized 48-hour session traces for final sim ingestion (optional, reduces uncertainty) — due 2026-09-08 (Sunstorm).
4) Pilot kickoff (technical onboarding + test traffic) — target 2026-09-20.

Please confirm the timeline and whether procurement wants both conservative & optimistic bound included in the SOW, or just the conservative table for contracting. If you’re good with these, I’ll upload the MAP appendix and drop the HubSpot deal note (HubSpot: deals/47892).

Appreciate the partnership — we’ll keep the econ transparency tight so FinOps has what they need for approval.

Best,
Dylan
